title: Services exports can help multinational firms keep goods sales moving during a global crisis
source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper linking U.S. firms' foreign goods and services sales and comparing multinational exporters during the 2008-2009 global financial crisis
geography: United States multinational firms and foreign destinations during the 2008-2009 global financial crisis

observations.period: 2008-2009 global financial crisis; paper published January 2026

denominator.unit: study-defined U.S. multinational goods exporters, mono-exporters, and bi-exporters; exact public abstract denominator not disclosed

goods_export_growth.value: multinationals that also exported services to the same destination had higher goods-export growth than multinationals that exported goods only

services_channel.value: the result was driven by sales of intellectual-property rights related to industrial processes, including patents and trademarks

foreign_affiliate_services.value: bi-exporters also had higher growth in foreign-affiliate services sales

domestic_services_employment.value: bi-exporters had higher domestic employment growth in services sectors

observations.method: Census CES working paper using newly linked foreign goods and services sales data and a triple-difference identification strategy combined with propensity-score matching to compare multinational goods-only exporters with firms that also export services to the same destination.
observations.uncertainty: This is a working paper. The public abstract does not provide the full sample, destination coverage, estimates, matching quality, or all crisis-period controls. The comparison concerns multinational exporters and does not establish effects for non-exporters, workers in every sector, consumers, or national economic resilience.
observations.subgroup: U.S. multinational goods exporters during the 2008-2009 crisis, separated into goods-only exporters and firms also exporting services to the same destination.
observations.counterinterpretation: Bi-exporters may differ from mono-exporters in technology, management, market power, customer relationships, product mix, or pre-crisis strength beyond the measured design. Intellectual-property sales may be a marker of firm capability rather than the sole crisis mechanism. Higher domestic services employment does not establish net employment, worker bargaining power, wages, or broad local benefit.

related_sources.claim: The Census Research Exploration and Analysis Tool provides the paper profile and summarizes the goods-and-services export comparison.
The official paper PDF provides the crisis-period data and method context.

boundary: This record adds a bounded services-trade-to-goods-export and firm-capacity pathway during one global crisis. It does not establish national resilience, worker welfare, consumer outcomes, causal generalization to other crises, or strategic autonomy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Census CES-26-04 landing page, official CREAT profile, and paper PDF metadata reviewed; underlying linked firm-sales records are not retained
